16-2051.title: Certified Public Accountant
16-2051.description: Certified Public Accountants must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Accountancy. To be licensed applicants must: 1.) Be 18 years of age or older; 2.) Be of good moral character; 3.) Earn a Bachelor's degree that meets Board of Accountancy class and credit requirements at an approved college or university; 4.) Successfully completed a course in ethics; 5.) Passed the Uniform CPA exam; 6.) Complete one year of accounting and tax experience that includes no fewer than 2,000 hours. Term: Licenses are renewed annually as of July 1.

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

16-2311.title: Engineer
16-2311.description: Engineers in Idaho are licensed by the Idaho Board of Professional Engineers and Professional Land Surveyors. There are two levels of licensure Engineer Intern and Professional Engineer. To be licensed as a Professional Engineer the applicant must: 1.) Graduate with a bachelor's degree in engineering or in a related field with coursework required by the board; 2.) Pass the Fundamentals of Engineering (F.E.) exam; 3.) Have four years of approved engineering work experience; 4.) Pass the Principles of Practice exam. Examinations vary by discipline and include: Electrical & Computer, Mechanical, Chemical, Civil, Agricultural, and more. However, Idaho does not license engineers by discipline. All licenses are for "Engineer" regardless of the exam taken for licensing purposes. Engineers working for licensed engineers or whose work is only for the internal use of a corporation or company do not need to be licensed. Term: Licenses are valid for two years before renewal.
16-2311.agency: Idaho Board of Professional Engineers and Professional Land Surveyors

16-2312.title: Engineer Intern
16-2312.description: Engineers in Idaho are licensed by the Idaho Board of Professional Engineers and Professional Land Surveyors. To be licensed as an Engineer Intern, the applicant must: 1.) Graduate with a bachelor's degree in engineering or in a related field with coursework required by the board; 2.) Pass the Fundamentals of Engineering (F.E.) exam. Examinations vary by discipline and include: Electrical & Computer, Mechanical, Chemical, Civil, Agricultural, and more. However, Idaho does not license engineers by discipline. All licenses are for "Engineer" regardless of the exam taken for licensing purposes. Engineers working for licensed engineers or whose work is only for the internal use of a corporation or company do not need to be licensed. Term: Licenses are valid for two years before renewal.
16-2312.agency: Idaho Board of Professional Engineers and Professional Land Surveyors

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-60.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2501.title: Physicians & Surgeons
16-2501.description: Applicants seeking to be licensed to practice medicine in Idaho must be licensed with the Idaho Board of Medicine. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Submit fingerprints and pass a criminal background check; 2.) Graduate from a board approved medical school; 3.) Complete at least one year of postgraduate training program acceptable to the board; 4.) Pass a board approved exam; 5.) Pass an interview with the Board of Medicine to review the applicantâ€™s qualifications and professional credentials. Term: Licenses can be renewed annually or bi-annually.

16-1021.title: Architect
16-1021.description: Architects must be licensed to practice in Idaho. Applicants for examination need to meet the following requirements: 1) Submit an application with required documents, and fees; 2) Graduate from a board-approved accredited architectural school; 3) Register as an Architectural Intern with the Board or completed the Intern Development Program; 4) Pass the Architect Licensure Examination. Applicants may be licensed by endorsement if they hold a current and valid license issued by another jurisdiction recognized by the board and a national council of architectural registration board certificate. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1021.agency: Board of Architectural Examiners · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-38.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-1031.title: Athletic Commission Combatant
16-1031.description: Combatants (amateur and professional boxers, wrestlers, and martial artists) who participate in an event must be issued a license with the Idaho State Athletic Commission. Applicants must: 1) Undergo review of age, physical condition, and ability; 2) Undergo physical examination including drug and blood testing; 3) Pay applicable fees. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1031.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1035.title: Athletic Seconds
16-1035.description: Idaho law and administrative code require all Combatants, Promoters, Matchmakers, Managers, Seconds including trainers, and Ring Officials to be licensed by The Idaho Athletic Commission at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. Athletic Trainers must also be licensed by the Idaho Board of Medicine to practice. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1035.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1034.title: Athletic Manager
16-1034.description: Idaho law and administrative code require all Combatants, Promoters, Matchmakers, Managers, Seconds, including trainers, and Ring Officials to be licensed by The Idaho Athletic Commission at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. The commission regulates all contests and exhibitions involving unarmed combat between individuals. Such events include all boxing, wrestling and martial arts contests or exhibitions, including simultaneous telecasts of any live, current or spontaneous event on a closed circuit telecast within Idaho, whether originating in Idaho or elsewhere. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1034.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1033.title: Athletic Matchmaker
16-1033.description: Idaho law and administrative code require all Combatants, Promoters, Matchmakers, Managers, Seconds, including trainers, and Ring Officials to be licensed by The Idaho Athletic Commission at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. The commission regulates all contests and exhibitions involving unarmed combat between individuals. Such events include all boxing, wrestling and martial arts contests or exhibitions, including simultaneous telecasts of any live, current or spontaneous event on a closed circuit telecast within Idaho, whether originating in Idaho or elsewhere. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1033.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2523.title: Athletic Trainers
16-2523.description: Athletic Trainers must be licensed by the Idaho Board of Medicine to practice. To qualify for licensure athletic trainers must: 1.) Graduate with a bachelor's or advanced degree from an accredited college or university; 2.) Pass a National certification exam; 3.) Submit two certificates of professional recommendation; 4.) Work under the supervision of a licensed directing Physician. Term: Licenses can be renewed annually or bi-annually.

16-1254.title: Audiologist
16-1254.description: Audiologists must possess a master's or doctoral degree from a nationally accredited school of audiology and supervised postgraduate professional experience. Applicants must also pass the national Praxis audiology examination or other appropriate examination approved by the Idaho Speech and Hearing Services Licensure Board. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1254.agency: Idaho Speech and Hearing Services Licensure Board · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

00-65.title: Ship Radar Endorsement
00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

16-1041.title: Barber
16-1041.description: Barbers must be licensed by the Idaho State Bureau of Occupational Licenses. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Document completion of the tenth grade; 2) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 3) Document completion of 900 hours of training for barbering, or 1,800 hours for barber-styling from a board-approved school; 4) Pass an exam. The holder of a current license in another state may also be eligible for licensure. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1041.agency: Idaho Board of Barber Examiners · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1042.title: Barber - Instructor
16-1042.description: Barber instructors must be licensed by the Idaho Board of Barber Examiners at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. All applicants for a Barber Instructor's license must: 1) Hold a current barber license issued by the board; 2) Have satisfactorily completed a minimum six (6) month course of barber instructing as a student in a properly licensed barber college; 3) Have a minimum of one (1) year of experience as an apprentice in a licensed barber college, or as a barber in a licensed establishment, within the last three (3) years; 5) Successfully pass an exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1042.agency: Idaho Board of Barber Examiners · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1043.title: Barber - Stylists
16-1043.description: Stylists must be licensed by the State Bureau of Occupational Licenses. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 2) Complete of two years of high school or equivalent; 3) Complete an approved course or an apprenticeship in cosmetology or manicuring; 4) Pass a written and practical exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1043.agency: Idaho Board of Barber Examiners · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1072.title: Cosmetologist - Instructor
16-1072.description: cosmetology instructors must be licensed in the State of Idaho. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Complete twelve (12) semester college credit hours or equivalent of required instruction; 2) Pass an exam; 3) Hold a current license as a cosmetologist issued by the board; 4) Have a minimum of two (2) years' experience as a licensed cosmetologist in a registered cosmetological establishment and complete a three (3) month teacher's course of instruction at an approved school of cosmetology OR Have a minimum of five (5) years' experience. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1072.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1071.title: Cosmetologists
16-1071.description: Anyone that practices cosmetology, nail technology, haircutting, esthetics, or electrology must be licensed in the State of Idaho. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 2) Complete two years of high school or the equivalent; 3) Complete an approved course or an apprenticeship in cosmetology or manicuring; 4) Pass a written and practical exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1071.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1073.title: Electrologist
16-1073.description: Electrologists must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Cosmetology. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 2) Complete two years of high school or the equivalent; 3) Complete 800 hours of training for electrology; 3) Graduate from a board approved school; 4) Pass a written and practical exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1073.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1074.title: Electrologist - Instructor
16-1074.description: Electrology instructors must be licensed in the State of Idaho. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Complete twelve (12) semester college credit hours or equivalent of required instruction; 2) Pass an exam; 3) Hold a current license as a electrologist issued by the board; 4) Have a minimum of two (2) years' experience as a licensed electrologist in a registered establishment and complete a three (3) month teacher's course of instruction at an approved school OR Have a minimum of five (5) years' experience. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1074.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1079.title: Haircutter
16-1079.description: Haircutters must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Cosmetology. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 2) Complete two years of high school or the equivalent; 3) Complete 900 hours of training in Hair cutting; 3) Graduate from a board approved school; 4) Pass a written and practical exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1079.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2071.title: Collection Agency Agents
16-2071.description: Collection agencies must be licensed by the Idaho Department of Finance. The agents who work for the collection agencies are registered on a quarterly basis. Credit counselors cannot operate in Idaho without obtaining a collection agency license. To be registered, agents must: 1.) Be an Idaho resident; 2.) Have no felony convictions; 3.) Have no outstanding bad debts; 4.) Pay a quarterly registration fee. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
16-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.
16-cdl.agency: Idaho Transportation Department · Division of Motor Vehicles

16-1037.title: Athletic Ringside Physician
16-1037.description: Ringside physicians for amateur and professional boxing, wrestling, and martial arts matches in Idaho must be licensed by The Idaho Athletic Commission. Applicants must: 1) Be licensed by the Idaho Board of Medicine; 2) Be certified to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1037.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2111.title: Child Care

16-1075.description: Estheticians must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Cosmetology. 16-2403.title: Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN)

To become licensed applicants must complete an approved registered nursing program, pass an exam, and and be licensed as a registered nurse. To become licensed as a Nurse Practitioner, applicants must also: 1.) Complete an accredited advanced practice, nurse practitioner program; 2.) Pass an exam; 3.) Obtain national certification. To become licensed as a Clinical Nurse, applicants must also: 1.) Complete a graduate Nursing program; 2.) Pass an exam; 3.) Obtain national certification. To become licensed as a Nurse Midwife, applicants must also: 1.) Complete an accredited advanced practice nurse midwifery Program; 2.) Pass an exam; 3.) Obtain national certification. To become licensed as a Nurse Anesthetist, applicants must also: 1.) Complete an accredited advanced practice nurse anesthesia program; 2.) Pass an exam; 3.) Obtain national certification. Term: Licenses are renewed bi-annually.

16-1151.title: Midwives (CPM)
16-1151.description: Midwives in Idaho must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Midwifery at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. Practice of midwifery means providing maternity care for women and their newborns during the antepartum, intrapartum and postpartum periods. The postpartum period for both maternal and newborn care may not exceed six (6) weeks from the date of delivery. Applicants for licensure must submit a completed application, licensing fees, and documentation acceptable to the Board. License requirements include: 1) Certification as a Certified Professional Midwife (CPM) with the North American Registry of Midwives (NARM); 2) Documentation of successful completion of board approved MEAC accredited courses in pharmacology, the treatment of shock/IV therapy, and suturing specific to midwives. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

Applicants for licensure must: 1) Graduate from an accredited architectural curriculum in a school or college approved by the board; 2) Complete or have started three (3) years of experience through the Intern Development Programor or have eight years of board-approved experience; 3) Pass an exam. The most common way to prepare for licensing exam is to complete a landscape architecture program at an accredited school. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1121.agency: Idaho State Board of Landscape Architects · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2301.title: Attorney
16-2301.description: Lawyers must be licensed by the Idaho State Bar to practice law. To gain licensure, applicants must pass the Idaho Bar Exam after graduating from an American Bar Association approved law school. The exam is given in February and July.

16-2075.title: Loan Originator Licensees
16-2075.description: Mortgage loan originators, mortgage loan processors, and mortgage underwriters who operate as independent contractors must be licensed by the Idaho Department of Finance. To be licensed, applicants must: 1.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 2.) Complete 20 Hours of pre-license education; 3.) Have no felony convictions; 4.) Not have outstanding bad debts; 5.) Provide Fingerprints and pass a background check; 6.) Pass a written exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2076.title: Mortgage Licensees
16-2076.description: Mortgage Lenders and mortgage brokers must be licensed by the Idaho Department of Finance. To be licensed applicants must: 1.) Register with the Idaho Secretary of State's Office; 2.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 3.) Cocument that the individual in charge of each office has minimum of three (3) years of experience in residential mortgage brokering/lending. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2073.title: Payday Lender
16-2073.description: Payday Lender in Idaho must be licensed with the Idaho Department of Finance. To be licensed, applicants must: 1.) Register with the Idaho Secretary of State's Office; 2.) Submit current bank statements that reflect a minimum of $30,000 in liquid assets and $5,000 for each additional Idaho physical location; 3.) Provide a History of Lending; 4.) Submit samples of all forms to be used in the lending process; 5.) Submit an application with required documents and fees. Payday Lenders licenses only authorize payday lending. Creditors engaging in the business of making regulated consumer loans or taking assignment of and undertaking direct collection of payments from debtors arising from regulated consumer loans must obtain a regulated lenders license. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2072.title: Regulated Lender
16-2072.description: Creditors that making consumer loans, or collect payments from debtors arising from consumer loans, must obtain a regulated lenders license. Regulated lenders are licensed by the Idaho Department of Finance. To be licensed, applicants must: 1.) Register with the Idaho Secretary of State's Office 2.) Submit current bank statements that reflect a minimum of $30,000 in liquid assets; 3.) Provide a History of Lending; 4.) Submit samples of all forms to be used in the lending process; 5.) Submit an application with required documents and fees. Payday Lenders require a separate license and fees. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2402.title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
16-2402.description: Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN) must be licensed by the State Board of Nursing. Applicants for licensure must: 1.)

16-1077.title: Nail Technician
16-1077.description: Estheticians must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Cosmetology. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Be at least sixteen and one-half years of age; 2) Complete two years of high school or the equivalent; 3) Complete 400 hours of training for nail technology; 3) Graduate from a board approved school; 4) Pass a written and practical exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1077.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1078.title: Nail Technician - Instructor
16-1078.description: Nail Technology instructors must be licensed in the State of Idaho. In order to obtain a license, an applicant must: 1) Complete twelve (12) semester college credit hours or equivalent of required instruction; 2) Pass an exam; 3) Hold a current license as a nail technician issued by the board; 4) Have a minimum of two (2) years' experience as a nail technician in a registered establishment and complete a three (3) month teacher's course of instruction at an approved school OR Have a minimum of five (5) years' experience. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1078.agency: The Idaho State Board of Cosmetologists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1032.title: Athletic Promoter
16-1032.description: Idaho law and administrative code require all Combatants, Promoters, Matchmakers, Managers, Seconds, including trainers, and Ring Officials to be licensed by The Idaho Athletic Commission at the Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses. The commission regulates all contests and exhibitions involving unarmed combat between individuals. Such events include all boxing, wrestling and martial arts contests or exhibitions, including simultaneous telecasts of any live, current or spontaneous event on a closed circuit telecast within Idaho, whether originating in Idaho or elsewhere. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1032.agency: Idaho Athletic Commission · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1084.title: Associate Marriage and Family Therapists (LAMFT)
16-1084.description: Associate Marriage and Family Therapists (LAMFT) in the State of Idaho must be licensed by The Idaho State Licensing Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists. Requirements for licensure include: 1) Graduating with a degree in marriage and family therapy; 2) 1 year practicum to include 300 client hours; 3) Passing a written examination. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1084.agency: Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1081.title: Counselors (LPC)
16-1081.description: Licensed Professional Counselor (LPCs) in private practice must be licensed by The Idaho State Licensing Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists. Requirements for licensure include: 1) Graduating with a degree in counseling; 2) 1,000 hours of supervised counseling experience; 3) Passing a written examination. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1081.agency: Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1083.title: Marriage & Family Therapists (LMFT)
16-1083.description: Marriage & Family Therapists (LMFT) in the State of Idaho must be licensed by The Idaho State Licensing Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists. Requirements for licensure include: 1) Graduating with a degree in marriage and family therapy; 2) 1 year practicum to include 300 client hours; 3) 3,000 hours supervised experience; 4) Passing a written examination. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

16-1083.agency: Board of Professional Counselors and Marriage & Family Therapists · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1141.title: Massage Therapists
16-1141.description: Massage Therapists are required to be licensed in Idaho. Requirements for licensure include: 1) High school diploma or equivalent; 2) Eighteen (18) years of age or older; 3) Good moral character; 4) Successful completion of a board-approved massage program; 5) Passing a nationally recognized competency examination in massage therapy that is approved by the board. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1141.agency: Idaho Board of Massage Therapy · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2545.title: Respiratory Therapists and Polysomnographers
16-2545.description: Respiratory Therapists are licensed by the Idaho State Board of Medicine. To become licensed, applicants must: 1.) Be at least 18 years of age; 2.) Complete a board approved Respiratory Care program; 3.) Submit two certificates of professional recommendation; 4.) Be registered with the National Board of Respiratory Care (NBRC); 5.) Pass a written and clinical exam; 6.) Pass the Board of Registered Polysomnographic Technologists Exam. Term: Licenses can be renewed annually or bi-annually.

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2404.title: Nursing Assistants
16-2404.description: Idaho maintains a registry of all certified nursing assistants. In Idaho, CNA certification requires completion of a CNA course including 80 hours of classroom and 40 hours of clinical training or one semester of an accredited nursing school program and passage of the CNA exam. Term: Licenses are renewed bi-annually.
16-2404.agency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare · 211 Idaho CareLine

16-1181.title: Occupational Therapists
16-1181.description: Occupational Therapists must be licensed to practice in the State of Idaho. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Graduate from an approved occupational therapy program; 2.) Complete six months of supervised fieldwork; 3.) Pass a qualifying examination; 4.) Be certified by the American Occupational Therapy Certification Board. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1181.agency: Occupational Therapy Licensure Board of Idaho · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1191.title: Optometrists
16-1191.description: Optometrists must be licensed by the State Board of Optometry to practice. Applicants must: 1.) Be 21 years of age or older; 2.) Graduate from an approved school of optometry; 3.) Pass a licensing exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1191.agency: Idaho State Board of Optometry · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-1182.title: Occupational Therapist Assistant
16-1182.description: Occupational Therapist Assistants must be licensed to practice in the State of Idaho. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Graduate from an approved occupational therapy program; 2.) Complete four months of supervised fieldwork; 3.) Pass an exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1182.agency: Occupational Therapy Licensure Board of Idaho · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2421.title: Pharmacist
16-2421.description: Pharmacists must be licensed by the State Board of Pharmacy. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Complete a degree in pharmacy from an accredited school; 2.) Complete a 1740 hour internship under the supervision of a licensed pharmacist, usually completed under the supervision of a college of pharmacy; 3.) Pass the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination (NAPLEX) and Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Examination (MPJE); 4.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 5.) Submit fingerprints and pass a criminal background check; 6.) Submit references of good moral character and temperate habits. Term: Licenses are renewed annually as of July 1.

16-2422.title: Pharmacy Technicians
16-2422.description: Pharmacy Technicians must be registered with the Idaho Board of Pharmacy. Applicants for registration must: 1.) Have a high school diploma or its equivalent and be 18 years of age; 2.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 3.) Submit fingerprints and pass a criminal background check; 4.) Submit references of good moral character and temperate habits. Pharmacy technicians who register with the Board will need to be nationally certified within 3 years by the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB) or the National Healthcareer Association (NHA). Term: Licenses are renewed annually as of July 1.

16-1201.title: Physical Therapists
16-1201.description: Physical Therapists must be licensed by the state. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Graduate from an accredited physical therapist program; 2.) Provide two references from individuals with personal knowledge of the applicantâ€™s character and ability to provide physical therapy; 3.) Pass a qualifying examination. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1201.agency: Physical Therapist Licensure Board · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2512.title: Physician Assistants
16-2512.description: Physician Assistants must be licensed with the Idaho State Board of Medicine. To become licensed, applicants must: 1.) Submit fingerprints and pass a criminal background check; 2.) Have a Bachelor's degree; 3.) Complete a nationally accredited physician assistant program; 4.) Pass a national certification exam; 5.) Be supervised by a person licensed to practice medicine. Term: Licenses can be renewed annually or bi-annually.

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2015.title: Apprentice Plumber
16-2015.description: Plumbers must be licensed by the state of Idaho. There are three certificates of competency available to plumbers in Idaho: apprentice registration, journeyman license, and contractorâ€™s license. Apprentice plumber applicants must: 1.) Be at least 16 years of age; 2.) Be employed by a licensed plumbing contractor; 3.) Work under the constant supervision of a plumbing journeyman; 4.) Be enrolled in or have completed a related training program. Specialty licenses are available in the areas of: Appliance, Water Pump, and Mobile Home plumbing. Term: Registration is valid for 5 years or for 3 years for specialty apprentices.
16-2015.agency: Idaho Division of Building Safety · Idaho Plumbing Board

16-1285.title: Backflow Assembly Testers
16-1285.description: Backflow Assembly Testers must be licensed in Idaho. Requirements include: 1.) Possessing a high school diploma or GED; 2.) Documenting successful completion of a Board-approved backflow assembly tester training program; 3.) Passing the American Backflow Prevention Association (ABPA) backflow assembly tester exam. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1285.agency: Idaho State Board of Drinking Water and Wastewater Professionals · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2016.title: Journeyman Plumber
16-2016.description: Plumbers must be licensed by the state of Idaho. There are three certificates of competency available to plumbers in Idaho: apprentice registration, journeyman license, and contractorâ€™s license. Journeyman plumber applicants must: 1.) Document a minimum of 8,000 hours of work experience as an Idaho plumbing apprentice; 2.) Complete four (4) years of approved plumbing apprenticeship school; 3.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 4.) Pass a written and practical work exam. Specialty licenses are available in the areas of: Appliance, Water Pump, and Mobile Home plumbing. Specialty licenses are available in the areas of: Appliance, Water Pump, and Mobile Home plumbing. Plumbing specialty journeyman must: 1.) Document a minimum of 4,000 hours of work experience as an Idaho specialty plumbing apprentice; 2.) Pass a written exam. Term: Licenses are valid for three years before renewal
16-2016.agency: Idaho Division of Building Safety · Idaho Plumbing Board

16-2017.title: Plumbing Contractor
16-2017.description: Plumbers must be licensed by the state of Idaho. There are three certificates of competency available to plumbers in Idaho: apprentice registration, journeyman license, and contractorâ€™s license. Plumbing Contractor applicants must: 1.) Hold an active Idaho State plumbing journeyman certificate; 2.) Document two and a half (2.5) years of experience as a licensed journeyman in Idaho; 3.) Pass an exam. Specialty licenses are available in the areas of: Appliance, Water Pump, and Mobile Home plumbing. Term: Licenses are valid for three years before renewal
16-2017.agency: Idaho Division of Building Safety · Idaho Plumbing Board

16-2014.title: Specialty Apprentice Plumber
16-2014.description: Specialty plumbers must be licensed by the state of Idaho and are only allowed to work in their area of specialization. Specialty licenses are available in the areas of: Appliance, Water Pump, and Mobile Home plumbing. Specialty Apprentice Plumbers must: 1.) Be at least 16 years of age; 2.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 3.) Be employed by a licensed specialty plumbing contractor; 4.) Work under the constant supervision of a specialty plumbing journeyman. Term: Licenses are valid for three (3) years for specialty apprentices.
16-2014.agency: Idaho Division of Building Safety · Idaho Plumbing Board

16-1211.title: Podiatrists
16-1211.description: Podiatrists must be licensed by the Idaho State Board of Podiatry. Applicants must: 1.) Be at least 21 years of age; 2.) Graduate from an accredited podiatric college; 3.) Complete at least two years of podiatric residency; 4.) Pass the national board exam sponsored by the National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners; 5.) Be of good moral character; Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1211.agency: Idaho State Board of Podiatry · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2061.title: Peace Officers
16-2061.description: All police officers, including conservation officers, must be certified by the Peace Officers Standards and Training program (POST ) within one year after they are hired. To be accepted into the POST program or hired as a peace officer, applicants must: 1.)

16-2064.title: Felony Probation & Parole Officers
16-2064.description: Parole officers must be certified by the Peace Officers Standards and Training program (POST ) within one year after they are hired. To be accepted into the POST program or hired as a peace officer, applicants must: 1.)

16-2066.title: Juvenile Probation Officers
16-2066.description: Juvenile probation officers must be certified by the Peace Officers Standards and Training program (POST ) within one year after they are hired. To be accepted into the POST program or hired as a peace officer, applicants must: 1.) Be a U.S. citizen; 2.)

16-2065.title: Misdemeanor Probation Officers
16-2065.description: Probation officers must be certified by the Peace Officers Standards and Training program (POST ) within one year after they are hired. To be accepted into the POST program or hired as a peace officer, applicants must: 1.)

00-05.title: Customs Broker
00-05.description: Customs brokers must pass an exam to obtain a license. Further information can be found at the US Customs Service web site: http://www.customs.gov/xp/cgov/import/broker_management/.

00-59.title: Purser
00-59.description: The Purser, one of a ship's staff officers, is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A Junior Assistant Purser requires no experience. A Senior Assistant Purser requires 180 days, a Purser requires 360 days, and a Chief Purser requires 720 days of service aboard vessels while performing duties related to the purser's office. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-59.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-1202.title: Physical Therapist Assistant
16-1202.description: Physical Therapist Assistant must be licensed by the state. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Graduate from an accredited physical therapist assistant program; 2.) Pass a qualifying examination. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.
16-1202.agency: Physical Therapist Licensure Board · Idaho Bureau of Occupational Licenses

16-2191.title: Real Estate Salesperson
16-2191.description: Real Estate Salespersons must be licensed in Idaho by the Idaho Real Estate Commission. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Be 18 years of age; 2.) Earn a high school diploma or equivalent; 3.) Complete at least 90 hours of pre-license education; 4.) Pass a national and state exam; 5.) Hold Errors & Omissions insurance; 6.) Undergo fingerprint background check. Term: Licenses are valid for two years before renewal.

16-2192.title: Real Estate Broker
16-2192.description: Real Estate Brokers must be licensed in Idaho by the Idaho Real Estate Commission. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Be 18 years of age; 2.) Earn a high school diploma or equivalent; 4.) Document 2 years of active real estate sales experience within the past 5 years; 3.) Complete at least 90 hours of pre-license education; 5.) Pass a national and state exam; 6.) Hold Errors & Omissions insurance; 7.) Undergo fingerprint background check. Term: Licenses are valid for two years before renewal.

00-61.title: Professional Nurse
00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-61.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2401.title: Registered Nurse (RN)
16-2401.description: Registered Nurses (RN) must be licensed by the State of Idaho. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Graduate from an approved nursing program; 2.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 3.) Submit fingerprints and pass a criminal background check; 4.) Pass a licensing exam. Term: Licenses are renewed bi-annually.

00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html
00-03.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-32.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

16-2034.title: Commodity Dealer
16-2034.description: Agricultural commodity dealers must be licensed in Idaho by the Idaho State Department of Agriculture. Commodity dealers have two classes of licenses. Class 1 commodity dealers licenses are required for dealers that purchase agricultural commodities by credit-sale contract or if the value during the past 12 months exceeds $250,000. Class 2 licenses are required for dealers that purchases agricultural commodities in a 12 month period exceeding $10,000 and less than $250,000. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 2.) Post a surety bond with the Department of Agriculture; 3.) Provide an audited or reviewed financial statement. Term: Licenses are renewed annually. Fees: licensing fees for a commodity dealer are based on the class type. Class 1 is $360, class 2 is $180. Renewal fees for a commodity dealer are also based on the class type. Class 1 is $65, class 2 is $35. A license which has expired may be reinstated for a fee of $500 plus the renewal fee if filed within 30 days of expiration.

16-2074.title: Money Transmitter
16-2074.description: Anyone that sells or issues payment transmissions through wire, facsimile, electronic transfer, or other transfer method in Idaho must be licensed as a Money Transmitter by the Idaho Department of Finance. To be licensed, applicants must: 1.) Submit an application with required documents and fees; 2.) Provide audited financial statements demonstrating a minimum net worth of $50,000 with a sliding scale to a maximum of $250,000; 3.) Deliver a surety bond to the Idaho Department of Finance in the amount of $10,000 on a sliding scale to a maximum of $500,000; 4.) Identify all Idaho locations where their business may be conducted. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2035.title: Seed Dealer
16-2035.description: Seed Dealers with gross annual seed sales exceeding five hundred dollars must be licensed in Idaho. Applicants for licensure must: 1.) Have an established plant, warehouse or place of business; 2.) Submit an application with required documents and fees. Term: Licenses are renewed annually.

16-2202.title: Education Administrators
16-2202.description: Public school administrators are required to hold an Administrator Certificate. The certificate may be used for service as a school principal, a superintendent, or a director of special education. The minimum certification requirements include: 1.) Pass a proficiency exam; 2.) Have a master's degree or higher (for principals) or doctorate degree or education; specialist degree or higher (for superintendents) from an accredited college or university; 3.) Have four years of experience working with students in a school setting; 4.) Complete an administrative internship; 5.) Complete a state-approved program of at least (30) semester credit hours or forty-five (45) quarter credit hours, of graduate study in school administration for the preparation of school principals at an accredited college or university.
16-2202.agency: Idaho State Department of Education · Teacher Certification

16-2203.title: School Personnel Services Provider
16-2203.description: Anyone who serves as school counselors, school psychologists, speech-language pathologists, school social workers, school nurses and school audiologists is required to hold the Pupil Personnel Services Certificate with the respective endorsement(s) for which they qualify. Public School Counselors must hold a Personnel Services Certificate and a Counselor Endorsement (K-12) from the Idaho Department of Education. To be eligible for the certificate and endorsement, an applicant must: 1.) Earn a master's degree in counseling from an approved college or university; 2.) Complete 700 hours of supervised field experience, 75% of which must be in a K-12 school setting; 3.) Submit an institutional recommendation. Public School Psychologists must hold a Personnel Services Certificate and a School Psychologist Endorsement from the Idaho Department of Education. To be eligible for the certificate and endorsement, an applicant must: 1.) Earn a master's degree in education or psychology from an approved college or university; 2.) Complete 1,200 hours of internship within a school district under the supervision of a certificated school psychologist. Public school speech-language pathologists must hold a Personnel Services Certificate and a Speech-Language Pathologist Endorsement from the Idaho Department of Education. To be eligible for the certificate and endorsement, an applicant must earn…
16-2203.agency: Idaho State Department of Education · Teacher Certification
